tools.name: check_environment
tools.description: First call on any machine. Reports data root, disk, GPUs, code checkout vs pinned commit, training Python (torch/CUDA/granitewxc), credentials, and what data exists, then returns ordered next_steps naming the tool that fixes each gap.

include_training_python.description: Probe the training interpreter (a few seconds).

tools.name: setup_code
tools.description: Background job: git clone the pinned Prithvi-UNet training/inference code and check out the pinned commit (pins.json) into PIPELINE_DATA_ROOT/code. Refuses to touch a checkout with local edits.

tools.name: setup_training_env
tools.description: Background job: create PIPELINE_DATA_ROOT/envs/prithvi from env/training-requirements.lock.txt (torch 2.12 cu130, PrithviWxC pinned) and install the pinned code into it. Jobs use it automatically. Run after setup_code.

depends_on.description: Run after this job_id succeeds (e.g. the setup_code job).

tools.name: get_dataset_metadata
tools.description: Get comprehensive metadata about available datasets: date ranges (training vs inference), file counts, available variables, spatial coverage. Helps agent understand what data is available without loading specific files. Returns info about both training (pre-2016) and inference (2016+) datasets.

tools.name: get_available_variables
tools.description: Get list of all available variables in training and inference datasets by sampling the first file from each. Returns variable names and coordinates. Useful for understanding what can be analyzed.

tools.name: github_repo_context
tools.description: Search the local granite-wxc repository for relevant snippets grounded in a query. Walks the local checkout to find and return the most relevant file excerpts. Use for conceptual questions about the model, training pipeline, config options, or data format.

query.description: Question or topic to search for in the local granite-wxc repository files

max_files.description: Maximum number of files to return snippets from

tools.name: load_by_date
tools.description: Load MERRA_PRISM dataset by date. Supports natural language dates like 'Jan 1, 2024' or 'January 1, 2024' or '20240101'. Automatically determines if date is training (before 2016) or inference (2016 onward) unless you override with dataset_type.

date.description: Date in natural format like 'Jan 1, 2024', 'January 1, 2024', '2024-01-01', '01/01/2024', or yyyymmdd like '20240101'

dataset_type.description: Optional: Override auto-detection. If not provided, dates before 2016 load from training, dates 2016+ load from inference.

tools.name: find_file_by_date
tools.description: Find the exact file path for a specific date without loading it. Supports natural language dates and auto-determines dataset type by year (before 2016=training, 2016+=inference).

date.description: Date in natural format like 'Jan 1, 2024' or yyyymmdd like '20240101'

tools.name: list_files
tools.description: List all available .nc files in the inference or training directory.

dataset_type.description: Which dataset directory to list files from

tools.name: load_dataset
tools.description: Load a NetCDF/MERRA2 dataset from explicit file path.

filepath.description: Full path to the NetCDF file

tools.name: dataset_summary
tools.description: Get a comprehensive overview of the loaded dataset: dimensions, variables, coordinates, units, and descriptions.

tools.name: list_variables
tools.description: Get a simple list of all variables in the dataset (QV, T, U, V, H, etc.)

tools.name: list_coordinates
tools.description: Get all dimensions and coordinate values (time, lev, lat, lon ranges).

tools.name: variable_info
tools.description: Get detailed statistics and metadata for a specific variable (min, max, mean, units, attributes). Optionally restrict to a spatial bounding box (e.g., LA County).

tools.name: slice_variable
tools.description: Extract and summarize a variable slice at specific time/level indices. Optionally restrict to a spatial bounding box (e.g., LA County).

tools.name: plot_variable_2d
tools.description: Create a publication-quality 2D map with colorbar and lat/lon axes, and return a downloadable PNG URL. Use lat_min/lat_max/lon_min/lon_max to clip the plot to a specific region (e.g., LA County: lat_min=33.3, lat_max=34.9, lon_min=-119.0, lon_max=-117.6).

var_name.description: Variable to plot (e.g., predictor_T_500, predictor_QV_700, target_ppt)

lev_idx.description: Level index when variable has pressure levels

cmap.description: Matplotlib colormap name (e.g., viridis, plasma, coolwarm)

vmin.description: Colorbar lower bound in data units. Omit for auto-scale.

vmax.description: Colorbar upper bound in data units. Omit for auto-scale.

lat_min.description: Southern boundary latitude for spatial clipping. LA County ≈ 33.3.

lat_max.description: Northern boundary latitude for spatial clipping. LA County ≈ 34.9.

lon_min.description: Western boundary longitude for spatial clipping. LA County ≈ -119.0.

lon_max.description: Eastern boundary longitude for spatial clipping. LA County ≈ -117.6.

tools.name: plot_data
tools.description: Create map, heatmap, line chart, or histogram plots and return downloadable PNG URLs. Use lat_min/lat_max/lon_min/lon_max to clip map/heatmap plots to a specific region (e.g., LA County: lat_min=33.3, lat_max=34.9, lon_min=-119.0, lon_max=-117.6).

plot_type.description: Type of scientific plot to generate

line_axis.description: Axis used for line profile averaging

vmin.description: Colorbar lower bound in data units. Omit for auto-scale.

vmax.description: Colorbar upper bound in data units. Omit for auto-scale.

lat_min.description: Southern boundary latitude for spatial clipping. LA County ≈ 33.3.

lat_max.description: Northern boundary latitude for spatial clipping. LA County ≈ 34.9.

lon_min.description: Western boundary longitude for spatial clipping. LA County ≈ -119.0.

lon_max.description: Eastern boundary longitude for spatial clipping. LA County ≈ -117.6.

tools.name: generate_workflow_image
tools.description: Generate an actual workflow diagram image (PNG) for training, inference, preprocessing, or a general process. Steps are auto-generated dynamically from process type, user intent (high/moderate/detailed), optional focus area, and optional YAML config context. Returns artifact URLs so the UI can render the image.

process_type.description: Workflow type: training, inference, preprocessing, or general

detail_level.description: Optional granularity: high, moderate, or detailed. If omitted, inferred from request_text.

focus.description: Optional focus area to emphasize: data, preprocessing, training, inference, evaluation, deployment, or model

request_text.description: Optional raw user request text. Tool infers detail and focus dynamically from this when explicit fields are absent.

config_path.description: Optional YAML config path to inject project-specific context (variables, date ranges, epochs, batch size).

title.description: Optional custom title to display on the workflow image

steps.description: Optional ordered list of workflow steps (minimum 2)

tools.name: compute_statistics
tools.description: Compute descriptive statistics (min/max/mean/std/percentiles) for a variable slice. Optionally restrict to a spatial bounding box (e.g., LA County) so stats reflect only that region.

tools.name: compare_dates_difference_map
tools.description: Compute date_2 - date_1 for a variable, generate a diverging difference map, and return stats plus downloadable PNG URL. Optionally restrict to a spatial bounding box.

tools.name: compute_trend_timeseries
tools.description: Compute multi-year daily/weekly/monthly trend for a variable and return trend stats plus downloadable line-chart PNG. Optionally restrict the spatial aggregation to a bounding box.

spatial_stat.description: How to aggregate each map into one value per date

tools.name: compute_monthly_climatology
tools.description: Compute and plot monthly climatology by averaging all days in a specific month across years. Optionally restrict to a spatial bounding box.

var_name.description: Variable to analyze (e.g., target_tmax for PRISM maximum temperature)

lev_idx.description: Pressure-level index when variable has multiple levels

cmap.description: Matplotlib colormap name (e.g., coolwarm, plasma, RdYlBu_r)

vmin.description: Optional: Colorbar lower bound to fix scale across comparisons

vmax.description: Optional: Colorbar upper bound to fix scale across comparisons

start_year.description: Optional: Start year to filter climatology (e.g., 2016).

end_year.description: Optional: End year to filter climatology (e.g., 2025).

tools.name: compute_seasonal_climatology
tools.description: Compute and plot seasonal climatology by averaging all days in a season across all years. Optionally restrict to a spatial bounding box.

season.description: Season code: DJF=winter, MAM=spring, JJA=summer, SON=fall

start_year.description: Optional: Start year to filter climatology

end_year.description: Optional: End year to filter climatology

tools.name: compute_period_composite
tools.description: Compute composite map by averaging all days in a custom date range across years. Optionally restrict to a spatial bounding box.

start_year.description: Optional: Start year to filter composite

end_year.description: Optional: End year to filter composite

tools.name: check_raw_data_status
tools.description: Inventory predictors, PRISM targets, elevation, weights, and the code checkout under the data root; lists what is missing and which download fixes it.

tools.name: start_download_job
tools.description: Download or set up one pipeline input as a background job on the machine running this MCP server (files land under PIPELINE_DATA_ROOT, default ~/prithvi-wxc-data). Versions come from pins.json. merra2 needs NASA Earthdata credentials; weights is ~17.4 GB and sha256-verified. Poll get_job_status.

dataset.description: merra2 | narr | prism | elevation | weights | code | env | cordex | all (= merra2+prism+elevation+weights)

start_date.description: Inclusive start YYYY-MM-DD (merra2/narr/prism/all). Optional if config_path is given.

end_date.description: Inclusive end YYYY-MM-DD (merra2/narr/prism/all). Optional if config_path is given.

config_path.description: YAML whose dates.training range is used when start/end are omitted.

variant.description: Code variant for dataset=code: deterministic | stochastic_refinement.

depends_on.description: Start only after this job_id succeeds.

tools.name: start_inference_job
tools.description: Start a model inference job as a background subprocess over the date range defined in the YAML config. Returns a job_id immediately. Use get_job_status to check progress.

config_path.description: Path to MERRA_PRISM YAML config. Defaults to the standard MERRA_PRISM.yaml.

checkpoint.description: Optional: explicit path to a trained checkpoint (.ckpt file). Auto-detected from config if omitted.

tools.name: start_preprocessing_job
tools.description: Start a preprocessing/regridding job that aligns MERRA2 and PRISM data and writes NetCDF files. Returns a job_id immediately. Use get_job_status to check progress.

tools.name: start_compute_scalars_job
tools.description: Compute channel-wise mean and std normalization scalars over the training period. Must be run before training if scalars don't exist. Returns a job_id immediately.

tools.name: get_job_status
tools.description: Get the status, metadata, and latest log output for a background job (download, training, inference, preprocessing, or compute_scalars). Pass the job_id returned by start_download_job, run_training_pipeline, start_inference_job, start_preprocessing_job, or start_compute_scalars_job.

job_id.description: Job ID returned by run_training_pipeline (from its jobs list), start_inference_job, start_preprocessing_job, or start_compute_scalars_job.

tools.name: list_jobs
tools.description: List all known jobs (training, inference, preprocessing, compute_scalars) with their status, type, start time, and config path. Most recent jobs first.

tools.name: cancel_job
tools.description: Cancel a running background job by sending SIGTERM to its process. Only works on jobs with status 'running'.

tools.name: read_yaml_config
tools.description: Read and summarise an existing MERRA2 YAML config file. Returns the full YAML text plus a structured summary: case_name, num_epochs, batch_size, learning_rate, dates (training/inference), predictor_variables, target_variables, spatial_subset, and num_gpus. Use this before customize_config / create_custom_yaml to inspect what a base config contains.

config_path.description: Absolute path (or bare filename) of the YAML config to read. Defaults to the standard MERRA_PRISM.yaml.

tools.name: create_custom_yaml
tools.description: Create a customised copy of a base MERRA2 YAML config and save it to disk. Supports overriding: spatial subset (lat/lon bounds), num_epochs, batch_size, learning_rate, training/inference date ranges, num_gpus, predictor_variables (dict of var→pressure-level list), target_variables (list), case_name, and arbitrary extra_overrides. Returns the saved path, a diff of all changes, and the full saved YAML text. Input paths that do not exist on this machine are localized to PIPELINE_DATA_ROOT automatically, so always pass a base config through this tool before running it on a new machine.

base_config.description: Path to the base YAML config to copy from. Defaults to MERRA_PRISM.yaml.

output_name.description: Desired output filename (without path). Will be prefixed with 'custom_' if not already. Defaults to a timestamp-based name.

validation_start.description: Validation start date (YYYY-MM-DD). Must not overlap training or inference; required for NARR refinement.

num_gpus.description: Number of GPUs for distributed training.

predictor_variables.description: Dict mapping variable name to list of pressure levels, e.g. {"QV": [500, 700, 850]}. Replaces the existing predictor_variables and rebuilds input_vars / vertical_pres_vars automatically.

target_variables.description: List of target variable names, e.g. ["ppt", "tmax", "tmin"]. Replaces the existing target_variables and output_vars.

extra_overrides.description: Extra overrides applied after the named parameters. Dotted keys address nested values (e.g. {"dates.validation.start": "2014-01-01"}); dict values merge into existing sections instead of replacing them. Prefer the named date parameters for dates.

localize_paths.description: Rewrite predictor/target/elevation/weights paths that do not exist on this machine to the local data-root layout.

tools.name: run_training_pipeline
tools.description: THE ONLY way to start training / fine-tuning. Queues the case-scoped workflow in dependency order — training preprocessing → training-only scalars → validation/inference preprocessing → Prithvi fine-tuning (Phase 1) → tiled inference → evaluation — skipping stages whose outputs already exist; each job starts automatically when its predecessor succeeds. NARR only: refinement_type adds Phase-2 stochastic residual refinement on top of the frozen Prithvi model — Phase-1 residual cache → refiner training on the residual y_true - y_hat (diffusion or flow matching) → ensemble inference (y_hat + r_hat, ensemble mean and spread) → deterministic-vs-refined evaluation. MERRA has no refinement. Pass the deterministic base config, not a NARR_PRISM_<type>.yaml refinement template. All jobs are visible via list_jobs and cancellable via cancel_job.

config_path.description: Path to the deterministic YAML config (MERRA_PRISM*.yaml or NARR_PRISM*.yaml). Defaults to MERRA_PRISM.yaml.

num_gpus.description: Number of GPUs for training (also used for refinement training/inference).

save_every.description: Save a checkpoint every N epochs.

queue_inference.description: Whether to queue deterministic tiled inference after training. Default true.

evaluate.description: Whether to queue evaluation against PRISM after inference (and deterministic-vs-refined evaluation after refinement). Default true.

train_phase1.description: Fine-tune the deterministic Prithvi model. Set false to reuse the existing checkpoint at checkpoint_dir/<case_name>/last.ckpt (e.g. to only train a refiner). Default true.

refinement_type.description: NARR only. Adds Phase-2 stochastic residual refinement with this head. The base config must define dates.validation (e.g. NARR_PRISM_subdomain.yaml).

refiner_attention.description: NARR refinement with a UNet head only: false drops the bottleneck attention block (separate custom_<base>_<type>_no_attention.yaml, checkpoints and outputs). Transformer heads are always attention-based. Default true.

ensemble_size.description: NARR refinement only: ensemble members per day (default from the refinement template, 10).

refinement_epochs.description: NARR refinement only: override the refiner's num_epochs.

tools.name: start_evaluation_job
tools.description: Evaluate deterministic inference against PRISM on the exact canonical grid (evaluate_prism_inference.py): RMSE, correlation, bias and boundary errors, written as CSV, JSON report and a climatology/bias/RMSE PNG under path_experiment/comparison_plots/<case_name>/. Works for MERRA and NARR. Supports depends_on.

config_path.description: Deterministic YAML config whose inference outputs to evaluate.

depends_on.description: Optional job_id to wait for before starting.

tools.name: create_refinement_config
tools.description: NARR only. Write custom_<base>_<type>.yaml next to the base config: the deterministic config plus the Phase-2 refinement sections of NARR_PRISM_<type>.yaml, pointing model.phase1.checkpoint at checkpoint_dir/<case_name>/last.ckpt. run_training_pipeline calls this automatically; use it directly only to inspect or hand-edit a refinement config.

refiner_attention.description: UNet heads only: false drops the bottleneck attention block. Default true.

tools.name: start_refinement_inference_job
tools.description: NARR only. Run tiled deterministic + stochastic ensemble inference with a trained Phase-2 refiner: each member is y_hat + r_hat; writes deterministic, residual, members, ensemble mean and spread per day. Use to re-run inference (e.g. a different ensemble size) without retraining. Supports depends_on.

config_path.description: Refinement YAML (a NARR_PRISM_<type>.yaml template or a custom_*_<type>.yaml).

ensemble_size.description: Ensemble members per day (default from the config).

depends_on.description: Optional job_id to wait for before starting.

tools.name: start_refinement_evaluation_job
tools.description: NARR only. Compare deterministic Prithvi output (y_hat) with the refined ensemble (y_hat + r_hat) on the same dates and grid cells (evaluate_refinement.py), writing metrics, distribution/extreme diagnostics and plots under path_experiment/refinement_evaluation/<case_name>/<type>/. Requires both deterministic and refined daily outputs. Supports depends_on.

config_path.description: Refinement YAML used for refinement inference.

depends_on.description: Optional job_id to wait for before starting.

tools.name: get_gpu_status
tools.description: Return real-time GPU utilization, VRAM usage, temperature, and active compute processes for all GPUs on this machine via nvidia-smi. Use this when the user asks about GPU resources, whether GPUs are free, how much VRAM is available, or which processes are running on the GPU.

tools.name: preflight_check
tools.description: Check that a config's inputs exist for a stage (compute_scalars | preprocessing | training | inference) without starting anything. Stage tools run this automatically.

tools.name: get_run_manifest
tools.description: Return the provenance manifest of a job: command, config sha256, code commit, pins, interpreter versions, input inventory, and whether the run is reproducible (with reasons if not).

path.description: Or a manifest file path (e.g. one shared by a collaborator).

include_config_text.description: Include the full YAML text and pins.

tools.name: list_run_manifests
tools.description: List recent run manifests on this machine, newest first.

tools.name: replay_run
tools.description: Re-run a recorded job on this machine from its manifest: verifies the code commit matches, rewrites the embedded config to local paths, preflights inputs, and launches the same stage. Use dry_run first to see the plan.

manifest_path.description: Path to a manifest JSON (e.g. received from another institution).
